summary: Iteration 6 (workflow engine) backend testing. All 31 workflow_engine tests pass. All backwards-compat tests across the 8 required files pass (124 collected/passed in one pytest run — slightly higher than the 116 referenced because some files contain parametrized tests; ALL green). Source-level checks confirm: (a) TOOLS_SCHEMA has 137 unique tools including the 3 new ones (save_discovery_answer, advance_workflow_stage, mark_page_wired), (b) dispatcher in _exec_tool validates key/value/filename and sets ctx.workflow_state_dirty=True after each, (c) _wf_addendum is loaded once near GLOBAL CLASSIFIER block (line 9190) and injected into BOTH Anthropic system_prompt (line 9214) AND OpenAI messages (line 9255), (d) workflow_state persistence block at line 10451 runs only when workflow_state_dirty=True and writes via db.freebuild_projects.update_one with $set workflow_state, (e) migration: empty project => discovery, project with current_html>500 chars OR pages dict => surgical_edit. Gate semantics fully verified by parameterized tests.
critical_code_review_comments: freebuild_agent.py is now 10581 lines — well past the 700-line threshold. It is the single biggest maintainability risk in the repo. Recommend extracting: (1) the TOOLS_SCHEMA list (lines 89-1700) into freebuild_tools_schema.py, (2) the dispatcher _exec_tool() into freebuild_tool_dispatcher.py, (3) the provider stream loops into provider_anthropic.py / provider_openai.py. Tests already pin behaviour so refactor is low-risk.

mark_page_wired tolerates filename=='index.html' even when missing from project.pages dict (special-case at line 2460). Harmless for now, but if a project ever truly lacks index.html this could create a phantom wired entry. Consider tightening or document the carve-out.

Workflow tool imports (from .workflow_engine import ...) live inside the dispatcher branches — fine for cold-start cost but means the module is re-imported on every tool call. Hoist to top-of-file imports for clarity.

Persistence block (line 10454) silently swallows exceptions with logger.warning. For workflow state this is acceptable, but consider counting failures into a metric so silent DB issues don't accumulate unnoticed.
